mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 3.0% (historical 25th percentile) compresses discount rates for equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced cost of capital for corporate investments.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 3.0% over a 3-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.03 in the low-rate regime.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 4.5% signals restrictive monetary policy that increases equity discount rates and reduces earnings growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC > 0.03 in the tightening regime.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous month-over-month declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 1.0% signal weakening consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue visibility.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline >1.0% MoM, or interaction term coefficient >0 in regression.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.5%), a month-over-month payroll increase exceeding 0.5% signals labor market recovery, supporting corporate hiring and earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when UNRATE > 5.5% and PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM, or Rank IC < 0.03 in high-unemployment regime.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% month-over-month indicates strengthening economic activity, supporting corporate earnings growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when INDPRO > 0.5% MoM, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL below 1.5% annualized signals deflationary risk, reducing corporate pricing power and earnings visibility, producing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >55% of periods when CPIAUCSL < 1.5%, or Rank IC > 0.03 in deflationary regime.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous unemployment rate decline exceeding 0.2% and payroll growth exceeding 0.5% month-over-month signal a tightening labor market, increasing wage pressures and corporate costs, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when UNRATE declines >0.2% and PAYEMS increases >0.5% MoM, or interaction term coefficient <0 in regression.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising), a month-over-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% signals economic slowdown, triggering negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days due to reduced corporate activity.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is rising and INDPRO declines >0.5% MoM, or Rank IC < 0.03 in tightening regime.
